page: Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the EASv4 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores and 8 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) via Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The server features a dedicated CPU allocation and is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It includes 262 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate a split profile. While raw CPU compute metrics from stress-ng show poor single-core and weak multi-core performance, real-world execution tests present a more balanced average capability. Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, software compilation, and ray tracing all fall within the average category. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is average, though large-block uncached read and write operations are weak. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput consistently perform in the middle tier. Large LLM inference is highly constrained, with medium model prompt processing and text generation scoring in the bottom tier.

From a resource allocation perspective, this server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand proportional CPU scaling. By pairing 128 GB of RAM with 8 vCPUs, users avoid paying for unneeded compute capacity while securing a large memory footprint. The primary tradeoff is the weak raw multi-core processing power and lower uncached memory bandwidth, which makes it less suitable for heavy parallel compute tasks or large-scale machine learning.

The E16-8as_v4 is best suited for memory-bound applications such as relational databases, caching layers like Redis, medium-scale web serving, and software compilation tasks. It is also appropriate for enterprise applications requiring significant RAM but moderate CPU utilization.
